responses: After our committee discussion, my final position is that we should allocate the $5 million AI transition budget as follows: 35% to Automation, 25% to Workforce Training, 20% to Data Infrastructure, 15% to Employee Support, and 5% to Innovation Lab. I landed here because while competitors are seeing efficiency gains from automation and Riverton has clear room for process improvement, we can’t ignore that our employees will be directly impacted by these changes—investing in reskilling and AI literacy ensures our team can thrive alongside new technology rather than being displaced. The data also shows that strong data infrastructure is a foundational piece for any successful AI implementation, so we need to prioritize that to avoid technical gaps that would undermine our automation efforts. Employee support programs are critical to managing the transition smoothly and maintaining morale, and the smaller allocation to innovation lab makes sense right now as we focus on implementing core AI tools rather than experimenting with entirely new products before we have our basic systems and workforce in place.

I would recommend a 35% allocation to Automation, 25% to Workforce Training, 15% to Employee Support, 15% to Data Infrastructure, and 10% to Innovation Lab. This balance prioritizes immediate operational efficiency gains from automation—aligning with competitor progress and our room to improve manufacturing processes—while ensuring our employees are equipped with the AI literacy and reskilling needed to adapt, paired with critical support to ease transitions and maintain morale. Investing in foundational data infrastructure early will enable long-term adaptability, as industry benchmarks show this accelerates AI integration, and a smaller but dedicated innovation lab keeps us positioned to develop new AI products rather than just adopting existing solutions, creating a sustainable path forward for Riverton Industries.

Here’s what I’d tell them: I think the best way to split the $5 million AI transition budget at Riverton Industries is to put 35% toward automation for our manufacturing and back-office processes, since our competitors are already seeing efficiency gains and our operations have clear room to improve, 25% toward workforce training to make sure our employees have the skills to work alongside that new AI instead of being left behind, 15% toward employee support like career counseling and mental health resources to help people through the transition, 15% toward data infrastructure because industry benchmarks show that’s a foundation that makes all other AI work faster and safer, and 10% toward an innovation lab to test new AI products that could grow our business long-term—this balance prioritizes getting immediate, tangible improvements while making sure our people and systems are set up to succeed, not just chasing quick tech wins without planning for the whole company.

After our committee discussion, my final position is that we should allocate the $5 million AI transition budget as follows: 35% to Automation, 25% to Workforce Training, 20% to Data Infrastructure, 15% to Employee Support, and 5% to Innovation Lab. I arrived at this allocation after weighing multiple perspectives: while the data shows competitors are seeing efficiency gains from automation and Riverton has room to improve manufacturing processes, I was convinced by the need to pair that automation investment with robust reskilling programs to avoid leaving employees behind—hence the significant portion for training. The data infrastructure investment is critical because companies that built this foundation early adapted faster, and the smaller allocation to innovation lab acknowledges that we need to stabilize our core transition before pursuing new product development, with employee support as a necessary component to help our team through the changes ahead.

For Riverton Industries’ $5 million AI transition budget, I would recommend a 35% allocation to AUTOMATION, 25% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING, 20% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE, 15% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT, and 5% to INNOVATION_LAB. This balance addresses the immediate need to improve manufacturing efficiency, as competitors are already seeing gains from automation and Riverton has clear room for process improvement, while also prioritizing the most critical long-term foundation: ensuring our employees have the AI literacy and reskilling to work alongside new systems rather than being displaced. Investing in data infrastructure early aligns with industry benchmarks for faster adaptation, and allocating a portion to employee support acknowledges the real human challenges of transition that can’t be overlooked, while the small innovation lab budget keeps open the possibility of exploring new AI products without diverting resources from the core needs of our current operations and workforce.
